---
title: "PolyNN: the shape knob, worn inside the neuron"
subtitle: "Learnable orthogonal-polynomial activations vs ReLU on Fashion-MNIST — CHORA bench 4"
---

::: {.callout-note title="One paragraph"}
CHORA studies one object, $\Delta=\sum_n c_n\phi_n$, under three knobs: **size**
(depth/rank — dominates), **spectrum** ($\lambda_n$ order — killed twice), and
**shape** (the Jacobi pair $\alpha,\beta$ — this bench's territory). PolyNN takes
the third knob *inside the layer*: each neuron fires through a learnable degree-$d$
polynomial $\phi(x)=\sum_k c_k \hat P_k^{(\alpha,\beta)}(\tanh x)$ instead of ReLU.
ReLU is the network equivalent of a flat spectrum (infinite high-frequency energy
at one kink); a bandlimited container is a *choice*, and "fewer parameters" is
therefore a spectral claim — testable as one.
:::

## The headline, before the table

- **P-shape holds where it counts:** tanh-squashed Jacobi beats raw Hermite by
  +1.15 / +1.75 pp beyond the ±0.938 pp noise band, at both widths.
- **P-eff died as pre-registered:** a *total-parameter-matched* ReLU is at
  least as good as every poly arm — the "50–70% fewer parameters" claim is
  retired here, honestly, at d = 4.
- **The shape knob learned something:** $(\alpha,\beta)$ walked off Legendre
  to ≈ (0.40, 0.37) in every seed — boundary-vanishing weight, the neuron's
  own echo of the GP bench's Exp 1/4 edge behavior.
